note: Upstream runtime archives per target. A sha256 stays null until it is verified: the release operator downloads each archive, verifies it against the vendor's own published integrity data where the vendor publishes any, and pins the lowercase SHA-256 here with checksumSource saying how. A checksumSource starting 'computed-only:' means the vendor publishes no checksum or signature and says why. scripts/release/stage-runtime.ts refuses a null pin with RUNTIME_SOURCE_UNPINNED and a null url with RUNTIME_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. A postgres-<major> entry is a retained older PostgreSQL for one upgrade. libraries.<target> pins the distribution packages that layouts with vendorLibraries copy shared libraries from. URLs were checked to resolve on 2026-10-15; layouts and license paths were read from the archive listings. Entries with official=false come from a third-party redistributor because the upstream project ships no relocatable build for that target; their provenance needs separate review.

linux-x64.note: Only the libraries the staged ELF files need are copied (linux-libraries.ts computes the closure). glibc and libgcc_s stay system requirements: on Debian and Ubuntu libc6 depends on libgcc-s1, and the jammy libgcc-s1 itself needs glibc 2.35. Superseded package versions eventually leave archive.ubuntu.com; re-pin from the current Packages index (or fetch the same file from launchpad.net) when a URL stops resolving. Vendored OpenSSL, libxml2 and Kerberos need re-pinning when Ubuntu publishes security updates.
